name: COMP_048
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (77%)** · Ambiguous: Invasive vs Benign · Careful review
Benign remains in the 90% conformal set, though both models agree on Invasive [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 77%, Benign 16%, InSitu 6% | Invasive leads, Benign second |
| Conformal set | Benign, Invasive | Cannot separate these two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.92 / 76th percentile | Input looks typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model agrees |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 Invasive [F5] | Moderate neighbor support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 1, 5, 8) · ↑ invasive · Strongest concept association with invasive carcinoma [F2] · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 1, 5, 9) · ↑ invasive · Scored well above typical; also separates from InSitu neighbor · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 2, 7, 11) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; text-prompt score only · Weak
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 0, 5, 9) · ↑ invasive · Above typical, but poor spot check (3/20) · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Top-3 region removal drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60). Faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007): not shown to reflect the classifier. Necrosis and mitoses are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Benign (16%) stays in the conformal set; the call is not separated from it.
- Two of five similar cases are InSitu, so invasion versus in situ is unsettled.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 5, 8** — confirm tumor invading stroma rather than in situ growth.
2. **Regions 2, 7, 11** — review gland-forming areas for benign lesion versus tumor.
3. **Regions 0, 5, 9** — verify necrosis directly; its automated spot check was poor.
